### Disputed

- [Gold surged +1.25% to $4,121.80, described as "a significant reversal from yesterday's paradoxical -1.51% decline"]: The data bundle confirms today's gold price at $4,121.80 (+1.25%). However, the CNBC article dated July 9 states "Spot gold fell 0.4% to $4,060.46 per ounce by 0343 GMT" on the same date — this intraday spot reading conflicts with the Yahoo Finance futures price of $4,121.80. The report presents today's price as a clean reversal, but the CNBC article suggests gold was still falling early on July 9 (to a one-week low). The two data points may reflect different times of day (spot early morning vs. futures at report generation 08:45 UTC) or spot vs. futures basis, but this discrepancy is material enough to flag for a gold trader.
- [Silver described as "structurally weak relative to prior levels (~$69 in June)"]: The bundle does not contain a June silver price reference to confirm the ~$69 figure. Cannot verify the prior-period comparison level.
- [KOSPI "approximately 11% below the June 5 level of 8,160"]: The bundle does not contain a June 5 KOSPI reading. Cannot verify this comparison. (Note: not disputed solely because the prior report data is absent — the specific number 8,160 is unverifiable from any bundle source.)
- [Nasdaq fell -1.2% on July 8 (cited in the geopolitical section)]: The Yahoo Finance source (^IXIC) shows the Nasdaq Composite closed +0.2% on July 8, not -1.2%. The Yahoo Finance article text for July 8 ("S&P 500 fell 0.5%, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 1.2%") appears to reference intraday or an earlier session; the final close data in the bundle contradicts the -1.2% figure cited in the report's geopolitical section.
- [Report states "FOMC expects no changes to the rate until a cut in Q2 2027" (implied from Forbes source)]: The CNBC minutes article states "many participants indicated the appropriate level of the federal funds rate would be within or slightly below the current target range at the end of this year," while "many other participants assessed it would be above." The Forbes characterisation of a definitive Q2 2027 cut timeline appears to overstate the consensus from the minutes, which showed a genuinely split committee with no clear forward guidance on cuts.
- [Kitco BTC article URL cited as "https://www.kitco.com/news/2026-07-08/bitcoin-pullback-keeps-july-rally-alive-altcoin-breadth-weakens"]: The actual URL in the bundle is "https://www.kitco.com/opinion/2026-07-08/bitcoin-pullback-keeps-july-rally-alive-altcoin-breadth-weakens" (opinion, not news). Minor path discrepancy.

### Additional Insights

1. **The Brent-WTI spread ($4.42) is historically elevated and actionable.** The report notes the spread but does not trade it. With EIA forecasting $74/bbl Q3 Brent and the Hormuz situation settling into a "new normal" of intermittent skirmishes, the geopolitical risk premium is more durably embedded in Brent than WTI (US domestic supply is unaffected). A Brent/WTI spread compression trade — short Brent, long WTI — becomes attractive if a ceasefire framework re-emerges, as the premium would collapse rapidly toward the historical $2-3 range.

2. **The RBNZ hike to 2.5% with further hikes signalled creates a notable NZD/AUD long opportunity the report does not explore.** The RBA is under pressure after three cuts described as a "mistake," while the RBNZ is actively tightening. This monetary policy divergence (RBNZ hiking, RBA potentially on hold or reversing) is a direct driver of NZD/AUD upside — a cross the report ignores entirely despite covering both NZD/USD (+1.09%) and AUD/USD (+0.25%) separately.
